definition: Forecasting seizures before onset from EEG — harder than detection and potentially enabling preemptive warnings or stimulation.
details: Forecasting seizures before onset from EEG — harder than detection and potentially enabling preemptive warnings or stimulation.

explainer.lead: Seizure prediction forecasts a seizure from EEG before it begins, enabling preemptive warnings or stimulation. It matters because acting before onset is harder than detection but potentially more valuable.

tiers.eli5: Instead of shouting when the storm arrives, it tries to forecast the storm so you can batten down the hatches early.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to EEG to issue warnings ahead of onset or trigger stimulation. The main pitfall is that forecasting before onset is harder than detecting a seizure already underway.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally it is a forecasting task: from EEG, estimate whether a seizure will occur before onset. Its known limit is that it is harder than detection.

explainer.example: A wearable EEG system predicts an impending seizure and issues a warning so the patient can prepare or a device can deliver stimulation.
